propositions: REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY is defined twice in the MCP container's Config.Env with conflicting values: once from fetch-secrets.sh into the shared .env file pointing to the review-bot host path, and once from the -e flag in mcp_run_new pointing to the op-cert key path

The effective signing key relies on docker run's unasserted last-wins ordering to resolve to the correct op-cert path; if ordering were reversed, the MCP server would fail to start rather than sign with a wrong key
The .env duplicate is a dead override because mcp_run_new also sets the variable via -e flag, and docker run appends rather than merges --env-file and -e entries into Config.Env

The .env entry originated from an earlier single-owner compose layer but became vestigial after the blue-green autodeploy introduced the -e flag, creating a collision specific to docker run (unlike docker compose which merges values)

The fix removes the REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY emission from fetch-secrets.sh, leaving the authoritative definition solely in mcp_run_new's -e flag, while the review-bot service is unaffected because it keeps its own compose environment value
A new test must assert REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY is defined exactly once in the composed MCP container environment, with anti-vacuity anchors and mutation-check coverage to prevent regression
